The 2-vec construction is simple and intuitively improves on the asymmetric Gram–Schmidt mapping, while QuadMobius is an interesting higher-dimensional rotation parameterization.

The paper evaluates analytical solvers and learned representations across synthetic Wahba estimation, ModelNet10-SO3, inverse kinematics, and camera-pose estimation, including several relevant baselines.
Operation counts, microbenchmarks, gradient investigations, and treatment of special cases provide more technical transparency than is typical for a purely representational proposal.
weaknesses: The novelty of the central estimation theory is insufficiently established. SU(2) is isomorphic to unit quaternions, the 3D linear constraint is essentially the standard left/right quaternion multiplication constraint, the resulting eigensystem reproduces Davenport’s solution, and the appendix acknowledges that the noiseless two-point expression is equivalent to earlier estimators. The paper lacks a careful comparison proving what is genuinely new beyond a change of mathematical language.

The main empirical claims are not statistically supported: results appear to come from single runs, with no seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. Many gains over QCQP and SVD are small and inconsistent across datasets and metrics, so they could readily reflect training variance.

The model-selection protocol is problematic. For camera pose, checkpoints from the final 300 epochs are explicitly evaluated on the test set and the epoch with the lowest median error is reported. Inverse kinematics also reports the epoch with lowest median error without identifying a separate validation set, and the ModelNet criterion likewise leaves the selection split unclear. This can materially inflate the modest reported improvements.

QuadMobius is only defined under assumed distinct eigenvalues and a nonsingular reshaped eigenvector. Neither condition is enforced or empirically characterized. Near eigenvalue collisions or singular Möbius matrices, the map and gradients can be undefined or ill-conditioned, undermining the claimed continuity and practical robustness.

Comparisons do not control for representation dimension or output-head capacity: QuadMobius uses 16 outputs versus smaller competing maps. Important alternatives are omitted, and only selected ModelNet categories and Cambridge scenes are reported. The direct SU(2) baseline is discussed as performing poorly but its quantitative results are omitted.

The practical efficiency case is weak. The exact proposed general Wahba solvers are slower than established methods, the Möbius approximation is both slower and less accurate, and QuadMobius is roughly two-to-three times slower than QCQP/SVD in the reported map-level timings. The two-point operation-count advantage excludes edge-case handling and is not corroborated by wall-clock measurements.

The explanations for QuadMobius rely mainly on small toy gradient and dropout studies. The two QuadMobius variants allegedly implement the same forward mapping yet yield noticeably different results, without gradient-equivalence checks or repeated-run analysis. No implementation is provided, and several training and numerical-stabilization details needed for reproduction are missing.
